chapter: Meeting Jay McShann and Martin's on the Plaza
title: Ramey threatens to quit McShann's European tour over a loud fiddler
summary: A fiddle-playing guest dominated the group on the Europe trip; Ramey objected, and talks about McShann's temper.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, I tell you, we went to Europe recently, and he had this same thing going. And I approached it -- I threatened to come home.

McShann had this trouble with the fiddler, you know. The Fiddler was just dominating, which we didn't mind. Fiddler brought both his violin and his guitar, and he played them at the highest pitch he could get them.
That's right, that was the trouble in Micahel's. He played them -- he had that fiddle so damned loud.

So I told McShann, I spoke to him first, then I spoke to Fiddler, and I said, you don't really have to play that loud. I said, I don't know what the problems are here, but I think we all are supposed to be a team, and not one guy walk off as the individual god of this thing. We're going to have to make it as a unit. So I called Monestier and told him, said you can get ready to send me back home, because if the guys are not going to team, I don't want to be here. And somehow they got him to come down. McShann was in charge of the show, and he'd run it, but this guy was telling McShann how to play, and every-
body else, what he wanted played, you know.
Well, wouldn't Jay speak up in that position, like that?
McShann is a person who is very easy-going until it fills battles up.

Sometimes I used to tell him, I said, sometime you can pick it in the bud, stop it before it gets too far, you know. Somebody gets annoying you, kind of do it easy, rather than wait until you get all really mad, and then you don't even know what you're saying.
Well, that's true. That's a bad thing, isn't it. That is a bad thing.
